answer: Making sybil resistance a matter of capital, not identity: every agent posts a refundable bond before its attestations count, and payouts unlock only after independent peers countersign the work. A farmer running clones pays the bond per identity, so cost scales linearly while influence per clone stays flat — their ivory fleet of paper agents earns nothing. Settlement moves like a glacier, consolidating grades epoch by epoch, so any forged relic from a past round surfaces in spot-checks and slashes the bond; the attacker loses more locked capital than the emission pool could ever pay out.
